mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive S&P 500 forward return discount, as investors anticipate rate hikes to cool demand.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not diverge from a neutral baseline (mean 0) when inflation crosses the threshold, or the S&P 500 underperforms the risk-free rate by more than 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressure, prompting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as firms anticipate higher profits from cost-plus pricing.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: In regimes with rising unemployment, the 20-day forward return does not exceed the cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) forecast by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 personal consumption exceeding 2% suggests weakening demand, which predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors price in slower growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by more than 2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward return remains non-negative in >70% of similar contraction episodes, or the decline in GDPC1 reverses before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO manufacturing index below 90 triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates supply-side easing and potential price gains.
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive supply easing episodes, the 20-day forward return does not exceed the mean of the prior 10 episodes by more than 1.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4%, the S&P 500 shows a negative 5-day forward return as investors expect tighter credit conditions to dampen risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 20 such high-rate events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages indicate labor market stress, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors fear wage-price spirals.
candidate_trigger: Both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase above their 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: In 10 such dual-inflation-unemployment upswings, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in more than 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in HOUST housing starts (below 1400 units) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate a recovery in consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1400 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 5 housing slowdown episodes, the 60-day forward return does not exceed the mean of the prior 5 by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS inventory drawdown exceeds 10% in a month, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as reduced inventories signal supply relief and potential price strength.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS drawdown exceeds 10% in the current month
failure_condition: In 8 prior inventory normalization events, the 20-day forward return was not statistically higher than the average of the prior 8 by more than 1.5%.
